comment: One accent, one grey family, one radius scale, one 4px spacing unit. Each is stated here so the values below can be checked against a rule rather than against taste.
Light is a real theme, not an inversion: the same tokens resolve to light values and nothing below branches on the scheme.
A tap is signalled by :active, so a keyboard or switch user needs the same signal. The accent ring is offset so it clears the hairline it marks.
One disabled opacity for every control, so a control that cannot be used never looks like one that simply has not been pressed yet.
The canvas itself is painted page background. If the webview ever shows area outside the body box (viewport resize, keyboard, overscroll), it must be black, never the client's default grey panel.
Chrome is a bare row of controls. A title competes with the content for the same attention, and the surface is one operator's own machine.

Run state sits beside the connection dot rather than in the composer: it is a label about the conversation, and the pill is for writing. Kept in the DOM at all times because the script writes to it unconditionally. It is a pill rather than bare text because the phase has two channels: the dot carries it in colour, the words carry it in text. A reader who cannot separate the two still gets one of them, and neither needs a fill.

The mascot is the run state, not an ornament. It is a pure function of the same phase the pill reports, driven from one assignment, so the two can never disagree about what the run is doing — the same rule the terminal surface keeps (internal/tui/mascot.go: a run is a state machine and the mascot is a function of it). Its own black square is page-background in the dark theme and a badge in the light one, so one file serves both without a second copy.

Sessions live behind a sheet rather than in a permanent column. On a phone a permanent sidebar costs a third of the width for something looked at rarely, and the conversation is what the screen is for.
Belt and braces: the moment real content exists the resting screen is gone, even if a script path forgot to remove it.
The resting screen is one centred thought, the way a chat that has said nothing yet should look rather than a layout waiting for content.

The only message allowed a frame is your own. Right alignment and a fill are what say "you said this"; the reply needs neither because it is already the thing the whole screen is pointed at. The radius is 50% with a 48px ceiling, so one line closes into a pill and a paragraph opens into a slab with corners soft enough that no edge reads as a point — one rule, both shapes, no second declaration.

A tool call is a step in a run, so it is drawn as a step: one hairline node, one hairline rail to the next, and the output behind a single top hairline. No box and no fill anywhere — a filled box around every result is what made the transcript read as grey panels stacked on grey.
The rail is drawn by the step that is followed by another, so the line stops where the sequence does instead of trailing into the reply.

The waiting indicator replaces a label: three dots that take turns, so the surface is visibly alive while nothing has been written yet. The stagger is the whole effect — without it the three pulse as one and read as a blink.
Markdown in assistant messages is type and hairlines, never panels: the flat-transcript rule still holds, so code and quotes get an edge each and no fills anywhere.
The composer is one hairline pill on the page background, not a filled grey bar. A filled pill plus filled tool cards plus a filled sheet is where the stacked-greys look came from.
Settings and secrets are a task with steps, so they take the screen rather than floating over the conversation they will change.
Permission and question cards keep one thin warning edge and no fill: a tinted panel over the transcript was another grey layer.
No fixed overlays for the resting screen. The empty state lives inside #open as normal flow content, so there is never a translucent layer floating over the conversation.

--- Motion --- Everything here is under a second and either carries information or marks a state change. The frequency gate is applied first: nothing that happens a hundred times a day moves, and the parts that carry no information were deleted rather than given an effect.
One lift, shared by the waiting dots and by the mascot. Both are the run state and neither moves for any other reason, so a reader learns to read this shape as "working" rather than as decoration.

Messages and tool results rise in as they are appended, which is what streaming wants rather than one block that swaps. A fresh node runs this once on insertion, so nothing here re-fires while the same one is in place.
The resting mark is the whole point of that screen, and still it reads as dead. Giving the centre dash a slow pulse is the difference between "a place to write" and "a page that will not answer".
The live dot is state: a steady colour for an assumption, a breath for a measured one. That it changes when the state does is the feedback.
Settings settle in from a small rise instead of snapping into the layout.
No entrance choreography on the chrome itself: the bar and composer sliding in on load is what made the frame feel like layers arriving on top of each other. Messages still rise once on insertion.
Motion is a confirmation, not a performance. Under this budget the platform default is the right answer and the cheapest one.
Transitions off, visibility still authoritative: reduced motion changes how the sheet arrives, never whether it is there.
A wide window has room for both, so the sheet becomes a real column.

consts.name: PHASE
consts.value:
{
    "": "idle",
    sending: "thinking",
    streaming: "working",
    busy: "working",
    stopping: "working",
    awaiting: "asking",
    failed: "error"
  }
